certainty_reasoning: An unrecorded outcome is not evidence of no outcome, and Pietro's own view of the meeting is not recorded anywhere.
date_label: Met on a three-day trip to Nice with Harold Mellor, reported in a letter the editors date Thursday [? 12 January 1899] from Napoule.
summary: On a three-day excursion from Napoule to Nice with Harold Mellor in January 1899, Wilde met a young Italian named Pietro and wrote to Robert Ross that he was 'like a young St John' and that 'One would have followed him into the desert'. It is the stronger of the two Nice notices - a declaration rather than a description - but it is still only a notice: no surname, no age, no second mention anywhere in the correspondence read, and nothing recorded of what followed.

sources.quote: I met one beautiful person, called André, with wonderful eyes, and a little Italian, Pietro, like a young St John. One would have followed him into the desert.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, Thursday [? 12 January 1899], Napoule - reporting a three-day trip to Nice with Harold Mellor. 'Him' in the final sentence refers to Pietro; St John is John the Baptist, whence the desert.
sources.supports: The whole of the record for Pietro: a named young Italian met at Nice, compared to a young St John, with Wilde's declaration that one would have followed him into the desert; no outcome recorded

manuscript.repository: William Andrews Clark Memorial Library, UCLA
